idiom_name: pthread_mutex_t + pthread_cond_t with a re-checked predicate loop
implementation_notes: The classic structure is hand-written: a mutex guards the state, pthread_cond_wait/timedwait atomically release it and park the thread, and pthread_cond_signal/broadcast wake the wait set; POSIX states that a condition wait may return spuriously and recommends the predicate be re-evaluated inside a loop, so the guard and the signalling discipline both stay application code. Init/destroy pairing, cleanup handlers and error returns (EOWNERDEAD on robust mutexes, ETIMEDOUT) are the price of the manual form, which is why a queue is preferable when the guard is 'an item is available'. C11's threads.h (mtx_t/cnd_t/cnd_wait/cnd_broadcast) is the same shape at the same level of manual discipline but is optional, so portable components still ship the pthread path.
pitfalls: pthread_cond_wait is a cancellation point: the mutex is re-acquired before cleanup handlers run, so a cleanup handler must release it or the object stays locked forever.
Ignoring the return value hides EOWNERDEAD on robust mutexes, leaving the guarded state inconsistent while the thread believes it holds a valid lock.
A signal sent while no thread is waiting is lost, so the state change must be written before the signal - the predicate, not the signal, is the record of the transition.

variants.name: C11 <threads.h> condition variable
variants.implementation_notes: C11 standardised the same predicate-wait shape as cnd_wait/cnd_timedwait over an mtx_t, with cnd_signal/cnd_broadcast as the notifiers, so the guard loop and error handling are still written by hand but the dependency on pthreads disappears where the implementation provides the header. Because cppreference marks the whole header optional (__STDC_NO_THREADS__) and mainstream libc support arrived late, this variant is chosen for pure-standard C builds and embedded toolchains, not as a blind replacement for the pthread path.
pitfalls: If the implementation defines __STDC_NO_THREADS__ the header is absent entirely: guard the usage or ship the pthread fallback.
cnd_wait returns thrd_error on misuse (uninitialised objects, wrong mutex) and does not report spurious wake-ups, so the loop is the only defence.
